clue.text: Sick about the sticky coating for a medicated sweet

indicators.note: about means the coating word goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: paste is a sticky coating, as on wallpaper
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A cough sweet with a gummy coating, for when you are unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small lozenge, often medicated, dissolved in the mouth.

clue.text: Eyed an Elizabethan discovery on the table

definitions.text: Eyed an Elizabethan discovery on the table

parts.words: Eyed an Elizabethan discovery on the table
parts.note: a tuber with eyes, brought back from the New World in Elizabethan times and now served at meals

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a treasure from Tudor times laid out on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable with buds called eyes reached England in the sixteenth century and is a staple food.

clue.text: Folded papers for the engineer

indicators.note: folded says the letters of the word are bent into another shape

explanation.surface: Some folded documents handed over to an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a military engineer, as in the Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Descriptive of information on the prison grapevine?

definitions.text: Descriptive of information on the prison grapevine?

parts.words: Descriptive of information on the prison grapevine?
parts.note: secret information known only to ..., and also slang for being in prison

explanation.surface: Gossip spreading among prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged information is so called, and the word is also slang for being in jail.

clue.text: In a great way-or for one, by the sound of it!

definitions.text: In a great way-or for one, by the sound of it!

parts.words: In a great way-or for one, by the sound of it!
parts.note: meaning on a big scale, and as two words a big musical scale, played largo as the sound of it suggests

explanation.surface: Something done grandly, or so it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive or on a big level, the phrase describes something done grandly.

clue.text: Point to the mythical creature prepared for a walk

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
a troll is a creature of Scandinavian myth

explanation.surface: Someone directs a fairytale monster that is ready to go out for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a leisurely walk is a stroll.

clue.text: Bestial member of the grasping type

definitions.text: Bestial member of the grasping type

parts.words: Bestial member of the grasping type
parts.note: member read as limb, an animal's flexible arm used for seizing prey

explanation.surface: A greedy, brutish member of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's flexible arm is used to grip and grasp things.

clue.text: At the precise time, tenth had nothing to do, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put in an odd new order

parts.note: nothing is O, the round zero

explanation.surface: A tenth person had nothing to do at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: arriving exactly on time is arriving punctually.

clue.text: The previous occasion was the final one

definitions.meaning: the most recent time before now
the very last occasion, never to be repeated

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the most recent occasion and the ultimate one.

clue.text: An attempt to contain a nuisance on the wall

indicators.note: to contain means the attempt word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep a troublemaker under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a wall hanging is the thing found on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven hanging is typically displayed on a wall, so it is what is found on the wall.

clue.text: Joins, and in another way sets free

indicators.note: in another way says the letters of the freeing word are arranged differently

parts.note: unties means sets free

explanation.surface: Something both binds things together and releases them.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram works on a synonym of 'sets free', not on printed words, an older indirect style.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to join things together is to bring them into one.

clue.text: They need a foot or two to be got going

definitions.text: They need a foot or two to be got going

parts.words: They need a foot or two to be got going
parts.note: read as pedals worked by one or both feet to drive a machine such as an old sewing machine

explanation.surface: Things that only start when someone kicks them into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot-operated levers that drive a lathe or sewing machine need the feet to set them going.

clue.text: Letters open or sealed

parts.note: letters ... are an open document from the Crown granting a right, and the word also means plainly open or obvious

explanation.surface: A question of whether the post arrives open or sealed in envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters patent are an open royal grant, and the adjective means obvious or open.

clue.text: Not a sweet bunch-but fabulous!

parts.note: a bunch of tart fruit, and fabulous because it comes from Aesop's fable of the fox

explanation.surface: A grumpy group of people who are nonetheless wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparaging what you cannot have comes from Aesop's fable of the fox and the unreachable fruit.

clue.text: Educational capacity of a particular class

definitions.text: Educational capacity of a particular class

parts.words: Educational capacity of a particular class
parts.note: capacity read as space, the room in which a class of pupils is taught

explanation.surface: An assessment of how able a certain social class is at learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom in a school is the space that holds a class of pupils.

clue.text: Prepares hides after tops are turned on board

indicators.note: after puts the hides word behind the tops word

parts.note: caps are tops, like bottle tops
a tanner tans hides to make leather

explanation.surface: Someone tans leather once the lids have been twisted on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Capstans are revolving drums turned by sailors on a ship's deck to haul cables.

clue.text: Positions on the railway

explanation.definitionFit: Both posts assigned to people and halting places for trains bear this name.

clue.text: For instance, tortoiseshell vehicle moving swiftly

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: A tortoiseshell-coloured car speeding along.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper shell of a tortoise is an example of this protective covering.

clue.text: Beauty spot from which one can't take pictures!

definitions.text: Beauty spot from which one can't take pictures!

parts.words: Beauty spot from which one can't take pictures!
parts.note: a place full of beautiful paintings, where visitors may not remove the works nor usually photograph them

explanation.surface: A scenic viewpoint where photography is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum of paintings is a place of beauty whose pictures cannot be taken away.

clue.text: Like certain underwriters do!

parts.note: life insurers offer cover, and the word also means to make certain

explanation.surface: A remark about what insurance underwriters do.
explanation.definitionFit: Life cover is called assurance, and the verb means to promise or make certain.

clue.text: Soggy food. Is it archaic abuse for a Catholic?

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food
is't is an archaic contraction of is it

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about old insults aimed at Catholics.
explanation.definitionFit: An old derogatory word for a Roman Catholic, used as abuse.

clue.text: Acted as a solicitor for charity!

definitions.text: Acted as a solicitor for charity!

parts.words: Acted as a solicitor for charity!
parts.note: solicitor read as one who solicits, asking for alms rather than practising law

explanation.surface: A lawyer worked unpaid for a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading for alms or a favour is asking as a beggar does.

clue.text: Returning part as the governor appears

indicators.note: returning means the two words part as are read backwards

explanation.surface: An official reappears in his role as a regional ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Mounts a show of deportment

parts.note: mounts read as horses, which display their training and bearing in this equestrian discipline

explanation.surface: Someone stages a display of good posture and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: The equestrian event in which horses perform precise trained movements shows their bearing.

clue.text: One good quality? Such people have none!

definitions.text: One good quality? Such people have none!

parts.words: One good quality? Such people have none!
parts.note: read as people lacking a single moral principle, the word splitting as a single good lesson

explanation.surface: A quip that certain people lack even one redeeming feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without moral principles has no sense of right and wrong at all.

clue.text: Having a whale of a time at Speakers' Corner?

definitions.text: Having a whale of a time at Speakers' Corner?

parts.words: Having a whale of a time at Speakers' Corner?
parts.note: a whale blows water from its blowhole, and orators at Speakers' Corner in Hyde Park hold forth at length

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys themselves hugely at the famous London soapbox spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner is a spot in London's Hyde Park where anyone may make public speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranting at length is a sense shared with a whale ejecting water from its blowhole.

clue.text: Relationship between matron and nurse

parts.note: a hospital nursing rank between matron and staff nurse, which is also a family relation

explanation.surface: How a hospital's senior nurse and a junior nurse get on.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse ranking under matron shares a title with a female sibling.

clue.text: Sat around among the tangled reeds, and claimed

indicators.note: tangled says the letters of the words are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sat in the reed bed and made a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have asserted something is to have stated it as true.
